Welcome to Cue

Cue reads the other parts aloud and listens for yours.

  1. Script: add your play from a PDF or Word file.
  2. Rehearse: choose your role and a scene, then start.
  3. Settings: voices, language and your account.

        Your plays

          New play: upload it or paste it below, then save.

          Backup

          One file with all your plays, roles and progress. Keep it to restore on this or another phone.

          Upload a play

          A PDF or Word (.docx) file. Cue splits it into scenes and finds the characters.

          Text-based PDFs and Word .docx files up to 25 MB. For scanned PDF pages, run text recognition (OCR) before importing.

          One name per line. Only these characters appear under I’m playing.

          Put each scene heading on its own line (“Scene 1” or «Сцена 1»), write speeches as CHARACTER: line, and put stage directions in [brackets].

          Settings

          Account

          Sign in with Face ID or your fingerprint. No password.

          Signed in as

          Partner lines are made into speech by Google once, when you open a scene, and kept on this phone. Without internet, the voice above reads them.

          The mic turns on after your partner’s line.

          Claude splits each play you upload into scenes and characters. The play’s text is sent once for this. Turn off to keep plays on this phone only.

          How it works

          Cue reads the other parts aloud and listens for yours. A line moves on when every word is right; punctuation doesn’t count. Your plays are saved only on this phone. To keep a copy, use Backup on the Script page.

          Add Cue to your iPhone

          In Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. Cue then opens from its own icon.

          Install Cue

          In Chrome, open the ⋮ menu and choose Install app.

          If listening fails

          A box for typing your line, for when the mic can’t hear you.

          A quiet ping when the mic opens and when you get a line right. It keeps the iPhone’s voice and mic awake, as in hands-free mode.

          Switches the iPhone audio to media playback while your partner speaks, so the voice isn’t quiet after the mic was on. Turn it off if the mic stops hearing you.

          Try this only if listening stops between lines.

          Works with the setting above. Turn it off if the partner’s voice goes quiet.

          Speech log

          If listening or the voice stops, copy this log and send it to whoever helps you with Cue.

          How Cue works

          1. Add your play on the Script page: a PDF or Word file, or paste the text.
          2. On Rehearse, choose who you’re playing and a scene.
          3. Tap Start. Cue reads the other parts and listens for yours. A line moves on when every word is right.

          Keep Cue on your iPhone

          In Safari, tap Share → Add to Home Screen.

          Keep Cue on your phone

          In Chrome, open ⋮ → Install app.
